bull.b: Progress across multiple clinical programs reduces reliance on a single asset and creates several potential routes to future product revenue. Phase IIa execution for WVE-007 and FDA engagement for WVE-006 also provide durable development and regulatory catalysts beyond one reporting period.

A cash position supporting operations into Q3 2028 gives Wave time to advance clinical programs without immediate dependence on capital markets. This financial visibility can support disciplined development, preserve strategic flexibility, and allow value-creating milestones to mature.

bull.t: Differentiated RNA platform and broad opportunities
bull.b: A proprietary chemistry and modality platform can support repeatable development across several serious diseases rather than limiting the company to one therapeutic candidate. Its obesity, AATD, and liver-disease programs provide multiple opportunities to demonstrate durable platform value.

bear.b: Large operating losses and substantial cash outflows show that Wave has not yet achieved commercial operating leverage. Continued investment in development may require future financing or partnership receipts, potentially limiting capital allocation flexibility if commercialization remains distant.

The steep collaboration-revenue decline highlights the variability of Wave’s current revenue base and its dependence on partner-related receipts before product commercialization. Lower recurring or predictable revenue can make funding plans more sensitive to milestone timing and development outcomes.

Wave’s value creation depends on successful trials, defined regulatory requirements, and timely partnering decisions, none of which are assured by current progress. Delays, additional evidence requirements, or changes to the DMD strategy could extend the path to approvals and commercial revenue.
